findings.evidence: The finite-dimensional instance at line 38 is used only by the chosen `f.finite_hasEigenvalue`/finite-product proof (lines 52–64), not by the claim; `Mathlib/RingTheory/SimpleModule/Basic.lean:357–374` provides `isSemisimpleModule_of_isSemisimpleModule_submodule'` for an arbitrary supremum of semisimple submodules.
findings.fix: Move this theorem to variables without `FiniteDimensional K V` and prove it from the semisimplicity of the eigenspace `K[X]`-submodules and their supremum; retain finite dimensionality only where genuinely needed by the reverse implication.
findings.issue: `isSemisimple_of_iSup_eigenspace_eq_top` unnecessarily assumes `[FiniteDimensional K V]`; an arbitrary vector space spanned by its eigenspaces is semisimple as a `K[X]`-module.

summary: The diagonalizable-to-semisimple bridge is stated only in finite dimension although the implication is naturally dimension-free.
